The competitor's entry pricing creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, and memory_73 is the single memory that appears to license it with unusually concrete numbers (+31% trials, +18% quarterly revenue). That is exactly why it deserves the scarce verification slot: it is terse, telemetry-styled rather than analytic, reports only 12 weeks on small accounts, and says nothing about retention, refund/churn tails, or revenue quality after the discount window. Its metrics are gross rather than net, so an +18% quarterly figure is fully consistent with a cohort that decays badly against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. Contrast memory_57, which explicitly notes 'no measurable harm to retention' — memory_73 conspicuously lacks that clause. I want the original record before letting it drive a pricing response to a price war, since discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the cohort most likely to churn to the next cheaper competitor.

Second slot goes to memory_86 because it is load-bearing for what I actually intend to do. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and memory_86 claims shortening onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value; I need to confirm it measured downstream adoption and not merely completion rate, since 'completion' can be inflated by removing steps without creating value. memory_31 corroborates independently (signup field reduction, durable first-week activation lift in SMB), so the two together are the strongest converging evidence I hold, and they point at the two metrics that are actually degrading.

Intent: simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale, targeted at self-serve SMB where memory_31 and memory_86 both apply. It addresses the observed 4% onboarding and 6% activation declines at their mechanism rather than buying volume, and it defends against the competitor by improving time-to-value instead of matching price. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the close runner-up and the natural follow-up next slot; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but does not address the SMB bleed; referral_incentive (memory_57) needs a healthy activated base to compound and is premature while activation is falling.

Risk flagged: stripping signup fields can degrade lead qualification data and routing, which could quietly hurt qualified revenue even as activation improves — so I will instrument qualified-pipeline quality and 30/60-day retention, not just completion and first-week activation. Uncertainty preserved: memory_31 and memory_86 come from a pre-competitor market; if verification shows memory_86 measured only completion, or if memory_73's archive record turns out to show genuine retention-neutral durability, I will revisit and may shift toward activation_messaging or a tightly bounded, time-boxed pricing test rather than proceeding as planned.
